skill.name: audit-website
skill.description: Audit websites with the squirrelscan CLI for SEO, technical, content, performance, accessibility, and security issues.
skill.summary: Run squirrelscan website audits and produce LLM-ready site health reports.
skill.author: squirrelscan
skill.license: See LICENSE file in repository root

security_audit.summary: Most URL and Markdown backtick findings are documentation examples and false positives. The remote installation guidance is confirmed risky because it recommends curl-to-bash and PowerShell irm-to-iex execution. The skill also needs consent boundaries before inspecting local context, starting development servers, or crawling live sites.

remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash and irm-to-iex guidance with signed release downloads, checksum verification, and explicit user confirmation.
Ask for a target URL first and require consent before reading environment variables, project metadata, memory, or local code references.
Require explicit user approval before starting or restarting any local development server or project script.
Document all files created under hidden home paths and require confirmation before modifying PATH, permissions, or user-local binaries.
Require confirmation that the user owns the target site or has permission to crawl it before running an audit.

This can expose local metadata or execute project scripts before the user has approved that scope.

semantic_findings.title: No Authorization Check Before Live Website Crawling
semantic_findings.description: The skill prefers live websites and suggests choosing live targets when available, but it does not require confirmation that the user owns or may crawl the site. This can enable unwanted third-party site crawling.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines prefer live targets and suggest them to the user. The risk is contextual because authorized live-site auditing is also a legitimate use case.

content.value_statement: Website issues are hard to prioritize across SEO, performance, accessibility, and security. This skill runs squirrelscan and turns crawl results into concise reports for AI-assisted fixes.
actual_capabilities: Runs squirrel audit commands against a provided website URL.
Generates LLM-format reports with scores, issue categories, affected pages, and fixes.
Checks SEO metadata, broken links, crawlability, performance, accessibility, and security rules.
Supports refreshed, resumed, and larger crawls through documented squirrel options.
Explains report findings and helps prioritize remediation steps.
Reuses prior audit IDs with squirrel report when available.
limitations: Requires the squirrel CLI to be installed and available in PATH.
Audits depend on network access and target site availability.
Large sites can take several minutes and may be capped by page limits.
Live site results can differ from local development builds.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Marketing Site for Launch
use_cases.description: Run a website audit before launch and prioritize SEO, accessibility, and performance fixes.

use_cases.title: Debug Technical SEO Regressions
use_cases.description: Compare fresh audit results after a release and identify broken links, redirects, and metadata issues.

use_cases.title: Create a Site Health Backlog
use_cases.description: Turn audit findings into a prioritized remediation list with affected pages and clear next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Quick Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit https://example.com with squirrelscan and summarize the top issues in LLM format.

prompt_templates.title: Check After a Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a fresh squirrelscan audit for <url> with refresh enabled, then highlight the highest priority changes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Large Content Site
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit <url> with a higher page limit, group findings by category, and list repeated issues first.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Previous Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Use audit ID <audit-id> to export an LLM report, identify root causes, and create a remediation plan.

output_examples.input: Audit a marketing site for launch readiness.
output: Overall health score with category scores.
Top SEO, accessibility, performance, and security issues.

output_examples.input: Review a site after fixing broken links.
output: Fresh crawl summary and remaining link failures.
Warnings that changed since the previous audit.

output_examples.input: Explain a squirrelscan LLM report to a product team.
output: Plain language summary of the most important findings.

best_practices: Ask the user to confirm the target URL before crawling when multiple options are found.
Use LLM format for analysis and keep console output for progress only.
Rerun with refresh after fixes to confirm changes on the same target.
anti_patterns: Do not audit third-party sites without permission.
Do not start local servers or inspect environment variables without user approval.
Do not treat the health score as a complete security assessment.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits website health across SEO, technical quality, content, accessibility, performance, links, and security checks.

faq.question: Does it require another tool?
faq.answer: Yes. The squirrel CLI must be installed and available in PATH before the skill can run audits.

faq.question: Can it audit local development sites?
faq.answer: Yes, if the local site is running and reachable by URL. The user should approve any local server startup.

faq.question: Can it audit live websites?
faq.answer: Yes. The user should confirm they own the site or have permission to crawl it.

faq.question: What output is best for AI analysis?
faq.answer: The LLM report format is best because it is compact and includes scores, issue groups, affected pages, and fixes.

faq.question: Does it fix issues automatically?
faq.answer: No. It reports issues and recommendations. Code changes still require user approval and project-specific implementation.
